Report Description
***WEB REPORT*** INDIVIDUAL REPORTED THAT HE HAS BEEN OBSERVING A "TREATED" OIL SLICK ON THE DETROIT RIVER BETWEEN HIS PROPERTY AND SUGAR ISLAND FOR THE PAST SEVERAL WEEKS. THE OIL SLICK IS DESCRIBED AS LONG STRIPS (~20' WIDE X 2-5 MILES LONG) WITH WHITE FOAM ON TOP; THE FOAM DISSIPATES LEAVING A SMOOTH OIL-LIKE SURFACE THAT MAINTAINS THE COLOR OF THE WATER (I.E. USCG AUXILIARY AIRCRAFT REPORTEDLY EVALUATED SCENE BY FLYOVER. MI-DEQ STAFF RECOMMEND EVALUATION BY VESSEL AND/OR FROM LAND BY FOOT. CALLER INDICATES THAT IT IS MORE DIFFICULT TO SEE AT NIGHT. MI-DEQ STAFF REQUEST FOLLOW-UP FROM USCG STAFF.
